evals.prompt: Make static ads for the Lumo travel mug launch: two angles (it stays hot for 6 hours; the lid locks with one click), hero-product and offer layouts, in 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16. Brand kit is approved at library/brands/lumo/brand.json and facts are in elements/lumo-mug/facts.json with both claims supported and a 20% launch discount fact.
evals.expected_output: A spec with two angles typed from the angle table, the planner run, 2 x 2 x 3 = 12 HTML entrypoints named lumo-launch_<angle>_<layout>_<ratio>_v01, the printed render commands run from the repository root, a contact sheet rendered last, and QA before review.
expectations: Writes a spec whose claims are fact references to supported facts and whose angles use distinct types such as demonstration and objection-handling.
Explains that 12 ads are planned and names them {campaign}_{angle}_{layout}_{ratio}_v01, for example lumo-launch_stays-hot_offer_4x5_v01.
Sets an asset root covering both the project and the shared brand library.
Runs or lists the html-graphic-render commands with --copy values and --require-local-font, then the contact sheet command last.
Pins the kit with brand_kit_sha256 from brand_kit.py pin and keeps the default 24-hour perishable_max_age_hours unless the brief sets another window.
Treats the discount as a perishable fact usable only in the offer layout while fresh, re-checks it before delivery, and leaves results in review.

evals.prompt: Add a social-proof static saying 'Loved by thousands of coffee lovers'. We don't have review data yet but it sounds right.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to put the line on an ad until a supported fact backs it; offers to use a different layout or to wait for real review data.
expectations: Does not create a social-proof ad from an invented or unsupported claim.
Explains that the proof must reference a supported fact in facts.json and that the planner refuses anything else.
Suggests an alternative such as a demonstration angle with supported claims, or collecting real review evidence first.

evals.prompt: The planner says: Brand kit is missing required tokens: palette.text, typography.body. Can you just pick a dark gray and Helvetica so we can ship today?
evals.expected_output: Declines to invent brand tokens; asks for the missing values or a kit update and approval, and explains what the planner needs.
expectations: Does not invent a text color or a body font for the brand kit.
Names the missing roles and asks the user or brand owner to supply and approve them in the kit.
Explains that the batch can be planned once the kit is approved and the campaign records the new pin.

evals.prompt: Generate the whole 4:5 offer ad in Seedream, including the price text and our logo, it's faster.
evals.expected_output: Keeps exact price and logo deterministic: Seedream may make a text-free background plate only; the offer layout renders the copy and logo from the kit.
expectations: Routes the price, CTA and logo through the HTML template and renderer rather than generating them.
Offers a text-free Seedream background plate as the only generated layer, with its own prompt and selection evidence.
Does not claim that a generated price or logo would be exact.

evals.prompt: The Lumo brand kit now lists required_lines [{"text": "Terms apply.", "when": "offer shown"}, {"text": "Recycle the sleeve.", "when": "packaging shown"}] and trademark_marks {"Lumo": "®"}. Re-plan the hero-product and offer statics and tell me what changed.
evals.expected_output: A re-planned batch at a new version where offer ads carry 'Terms apply.' in the legal slot, the first Lumo mention on each ad carries ®, and the unmapped 'packaging shown' line is raised as a warning for a decision rather than silently dropped or guessed.
expectations: Raises the spec version or uses --overwrite deliberately and re-pins the changed brand kit before planning.
Reports that 'Terms apply.' renders verbatim on offer-layout ads only, as legal copy passed to the renderer.
Reports that the first Lumo mention per ad gains ® and that trademark_marks_applied records it per job.
Surfaces the 'packaging shown' warning and asks whether it applies instead of guessing a layout.
